languages.name: Hausa
languages.weak_spots: Less high-quality Hausa text exists online than for French or Arabic; expect occasional unnatural word choice, wrong gender agreement or missing hooked letters. Regional differences (Kano vs Sokoto vs Niger) are not modelled.

languages.name: Yoruba
languages.weak_spots: Tone marks are the biggest risk: the model may misplace or omit them, which can change meaning. Word choice for modern business terms is uncertain. Proverbs should be checked carefully; a wrong proverb is worse than none.

languages.name: Igbo
languages.weak_spots: One of the weakest languages here for the model. Dialects (Owerri, Onitsha, Nsukka and others) differ a lot and only a standard-ish variety is targeted. Expect English code-mixing choices and modern vocabulary to vary.

languages.name: Nigerian Pidgin
languages.weak_spots: Spelling varies widely and there is little edited Pidgin text. Ghanaian and Cameroonian Pidgin are different and not covered. Fast-moving slang may be dated or wrong.

languages.name: Moroccan Darija
languages.weak_spots: The model has seen far more MSA and Egyptian than Darija, so MSA or Egyptian words may leak in. Regional Darija (north, east, south) and Amazigh-influenced speech are not modelled. Latin-letter spelling varies between people.

languages.name: Egyptian Arabic
languages.weak_spots: Usually the strongest Arabic dialect for the model, but it can still drift into MSA in formal tone. Upper Egyptian (Sa'idi) is not covered.

languages.name: Saudi Arabic
languages.weak_spots: Saudi Arabic is varied (Najdi, Hijazi, southern, eastern). Only urban Najdi with some Hijazi is targeted; the model may blend in general Gulf (Emirati/Kuwaiti) words. Latin-letter Saudi texting is less common, so spelling is less settled.

languages.name: Levantine Arabic
languages.weak_spots: 'Levantine' covers four countries; output aims for common ground and may sound slightly 'off' to a Lebanese or Palestinian ear. Choosing between Lebanese French code-mixing and Jordanian/Syrian norms is not configurable.

languages.name: Swahili
languages.weak_spots: Better covered than the Nigerian languages, but Kenyan and Tanzanian preferences differ and the output may mix them. Noun-class agreement errors can still appear.

languages.name: French
languages.weak_spots: Strong overall. West African, Belgian, Swiss and Canadian French differ in vocabulary and are not separate options yet.
